finding: Minimal-vs-systematic needs an honest minimal arm; M0 contains leakage so M0 vs S would mix leakage removal with preparation quality
evidence_value: M0 88 / M1 46 / S 42 Tier-1 design columns
decision: Arms M0 (naive, leakage), M1 = M0 + P03, S = P01-P13; headline comparison M1 vs S, M0 -> M1 is the leak gate; same estimator for all arms (basic-model rule)
alternatives_rejected: M0 vs S as headline (confounds leakage with preparation); separate model per arm
check_note: Re-run: all-False pipeline equals an independently written naive M0 to 1.5e-15

finding: A naive analyst recodes 7/9/77/99/... everywhere and builds the label from the recoded data
evidence_value: 2,003 valid feature values wiped (training part, Tier 1); 29 HbA1c positives lost; 6 L_comb flips (965 vs 971)
decision: P02 is a Switch: off = blanket recode (M0 behaviour), on = codebook codes per variable; the training label of an arm follows its P02 setting, evaluation always uses the frozen L_comb
alternatives_rejected: Off = no recode at all (would not be what M0 does); evaluate against the naive label (would hide the damage)
check_note: Asserted flips == 6 and HbA1c positives lost == 29 (S3 metrics: 6/971, 29/721)

finding: The XPT zero artefact is numerically harmless but breaks equality tests on zero
evidence_value: 3,630 artefact cells (PAD810Q 2,556, PAD790Q 939, INDFMMPI 93, INDFMPIR 38, PAD680 4); without P01 the 939 non-exercisers lose their 0 weekly minutes
decision: P01 as a stateless step with mask() (NaN preserved); its effect is measured jointly with P02 (block B1)
check_note: NaN count unchanged after P01 (asserted in nhanes_io.fix_xpt)

finding: Leakage and audit-only variables must be removed by the S1 availability rule, not by judgement per variable
evidence_value: P03 removes 22 of 52 Tier-1 columns (8 leak, 3 audit, 5 optional, 2 cohort filter, 2 redundancy, 2 side)
decision: P03 keeps spec features with admissible T1 (Tier 1) or T1/T2 (Tier 2); explicit S1 list asserted; T1-minus-care arm drops BPQ020/BPQ080 in addition
alternatives_rejected: Manual exclusion list; keeping MCQ history items (care-contact traces outside the frozen T1 list)
check_note: Asserted: every excluded column has admissible N; LBXGLU, DIQ050, DIQ070, DID040, DID060, DIQ160, DIQ180, RIDRETH3, HIQ011, HUQ030 excluded

finding: Physical-activity duration is skipped by design when frequency is 0; median imputation would give non-exercisers a typical session
evidence_value: 939 moderate / 2,556 vigorous structural gaps; naive median 45 min; 20.5% have 0 weekly moderate minutes
decision: P04 = mean of the 3 SBP, DBP and pulse readings plus weekly moderate and vigorous minutes (frequency x unit x duration, 0 if frequency 0); deviation: the original plan named only BP means
alternatives_rejected: Median-impute duration; keep frequency, unit and duration as separate columns
check_note: Recomputed in-notebook; P04 is stateless (random-y assertion)

finding: Weight, height and BMI are formula-linked; VIF alone is not a reason to delete (O'Brien 2007)
evidence_value: In-fold VIF: weight 69.5, BMI 62.3 -> after pruning BMI 9.7, max 9.7; 6 raw BP readings 8.7-11.7
decision: P05 iterative VIF > 10 pruning fitted in each training fold, BMI and waist (or WHtR) protected; drops weight only; L2 as second defence
alternatives_rejected: Drop weight, height, hip and arm a priori (DAJ list); L1 selection (unstable under collinearity)

finding: Indicators only help where missingness is informative (MNAR-suspect)
evidence_value: Prevalence missing vs observed: waist 29.8% vs 16.4%; income 17.4% vs 16.9%; BP 19.4% vs 16.9%; TC 19.9% vs 16.8%
decision: P06 indicators for INDFMPIR, BMXWAIST, bp_sys_mean, LBXTC; P07 flags age 80+ and PIR 5+; B4 hypothesis marked descriptive_seen because this table was seen before the lock
alternatives_rejected: Indicators for every column (bias under MAR, Groenwold 2012); no indicators
check_note: Table recomputed on the training part

finding: Age and BMI (HDL, TC in Tier 2) are monotone but curved; activity minutes are heavily skewed
evidence_value: skew pa_vig 12.1, pa_mod 6.0, hip 1.13 -> 0.42/-0.12/0.00 after Yeo-Johnson; no category below 2%
decision: P13 SplineTransformer(n_knots=4, degree=3, quantile knots, linear extrapolation) for age and BMI (+HDL, TC in Tier 2); P08 Yeo-Johnson in-fold for |skew| > 1 on non-splined columns; P09 scaling; P10 rare grouping
alternatives_rejected: Restricted cubic splines via patsy (extra dependency); log transform (not defined at 0 minutes); interaction terms (not detected in §4.12)
check_note: Tree predictions identical with and without P08/P09 (asserted)

finding: Class weights change calibration; survey weights change the target population and cut effective n
evidence_value: prevalence 0.170; positives x2.95; Kish deff 1.54 (effective n 2,968 of 4,584)
decision: S includes P11 class_weight='balanced' and P12 WTPH2YR/mean; their effects are isolated by S-B6a and S-B6b
alternatives_rejected: SMOTE (breaks calibration and survey design); threshold moving only

finding: A splined BMI has no single coefficient, so coefficient stability needs unsplined companions
evidence_value: S-linear and S-linear-B3 differ only in P04/P05
decision: Add S-linear-B3; B3b/H2b compare per-SD BMI coefficient SDs on S-linear (and M1)
alternatives_rejected: Use splined S directly (no comparable coefficient)

finding: Block hypotheses must be fixed before any ablation result exists
evidence_value: B1-B6, B2t and P14 with direction, magnitude, SESOI, falsifier, prior_exposure and operational verdict rules
decision: Lock hypotheses.md with SHA-256 and a dedicated commit before the first exp(S7) commit; later changes only as post-lock amendments
alternatives_rejected: Lock after FAST results (would not be a pre-registration)
check_note: SHA-256 recomputed from the lock commit in §6.11

finding: Design statistics must not use the hold-out
decision: evalkit.make_holdout called once (first use in S6); all S6 tables and all S7 CV use the training part only
alternatives_rejected: Design statistics on the full cohort
check_note: Hash verified on every later call
